notes.title: Early December update
notes.content:
Hello, everyone! 

2021 is quickly coming to an end, and there aren't enough hours in a day to cover everything we've 
already begun working on and everything we're eager to start with. Although we keep discovering 
new challenges every day, the enthusiasm and the work drive are running strong. We're very proud 
of the development progress so far, and we are excited to let you in on a few newest changes to 
Pastel:

[olist]
[*] Looking back at the initial idea of creating a visually pleasing adventure puzzle experience, 
we've noticed a slight disbalance between the puzzle and the adventure aspect. So what did 
we do to add more 'venture' into the adventure? A whole [b]new mechanic[/b], of course! From 
now on, Pastel will be able to use [b]Possession - an ability to possess a nearby creature and
use its natural abilities to overcome obstacles[/b]. Ethically, of course. No creatures were 
harmed during the creation of this mechanic. 
[*]  How about the ability to interact with the obstacles in a much more elaborate manner? We 
got it covered! [b]Some of the obstacles can now be destroyed and repaired to complete 
given tasks.[/b] Ruined bridge ruining your fun? Nothing a few wooden boards won't fix. 
Collect, repair, and progress!
[*]  Additionally, [b]we have tweaked the labyrinth[/b] area with a few redesigns that we plan on 
implementing within the game.
[*]  We all love [b]collectibles[/b] for the sake of collecting, but in the world of Pastel, everything has 
a role. For that reason, we have assigned a more active one to each collectible symbol in the 
game. To keep it charmingly challenging, e[b]ach symbol now holds equal importance in 
solving narrative puzzles[/b]. Their completion will no longer be possible without all of the 
necessary pieces.
[*] [b]The Ghost World[/b] has woken up! This previously passive area [b]became richer for some 
interactive elements[/b]. You will now have the opportunity to explore it more while searching 
around for interactable parts of the environment and discovering their secrets.
[*]  In the end, what's all of this worth if it isn't looking its best? For that, we are working on 
improving the adventure with a [b]large-scale texture overhaul[/b] and showing some love to the 
third - no less important - part of Pastel: its visual experience.
[/olist]
A lot of the upcoming changes, and we are equally ecstatic to show you the progress we made on 
adding new levels... As soon as we get the new levels to cooperate with the game's environment. In 
the current stage, freshly added parts are clashing and require cleanup before the proper 
walkthrough. While we work hard on overcoming these obstacles, a friendly reminder that we 
appreciate your support! 

Keep up with the updates, and feel free to reach out for any questions you may have.

Thank you!

notes.title: Pastel: Blind Karma re-design
notes.content:
Ever since we first had an idea for Pastel: Blind Karma,
we have imagined a colorful, vibrant, dynamic adventure. And while we are well on our way to bringing that vision to you, it's always a good thing to leave some room for backtracking and addressing some things that could have been done better.

And we did exactly that! So what exactly did we do? Check it out below:

1. Pastel is now more enthusiastic about her mission! We have added a bit of a skip to her step by improving the jumping mechanics and the interaction with objects (It will now rely on indirect connection rather than simple, rigid animations).
2. We have even shown the shaders some love. They are now upgraded from presented assets to being handmade!
3. Color is love. Color is life. You will enjoy an improved color blend on grassy surfaces and ground textures. 
4. Overhauled! Trees and grass are all goosed up, making the entire image richer with a lot more tone. Real eye-candy.
5. Updates rock! No, really. We have updated our rocks. They are now much well behaved.
6. High five, but down low? Got a lower-graded software? It doesn't mean you should be getting a lower-graded Pastel: Blind Karma experience! We have optimized our textures to support your setup as well.
7. Prefabs can be fabulous! Especially the reconstructed ones. Tune in for an increased optimization and frame rate!
8. Cutting it close on the levels. Levels will now be more densely packed with a lot more puzzles to do! We need activities! What's all that empty space in between good for anyway?
9. Literary enthusiasts, rejoice! More puzzles mean more diversity, and more diversity means adding text puzzles. In these types of puzzles, players will need to collect different words/symbols to beat the stage. Each encountered symbol will be registered in your dictionary to be used to decode the messages! Venturing through the levels, you will eventually run into obstacles that can be destroyed only by choosing the correct sentence out of the suggested ones while using the symbols registered to decipher them. Sure, you can play it by chance and guess the answer but be warned! Making a mistake will lead to a reshuffling of the task into a new one.    

So much work to be done! Our development team is working hard to organize all of the prefabs and the content. And while there are some issues with the optimization, we are highly optimistic that we will keep it up on schedule! The biggest problem we are encountering is that the models are not cooperating and not functioning as we would want them to.

This means that assembling the first level correctly and offering you the best possible experience with all listed improvements will take more time and patience. Bits and pieces need to be put into place. Nothing is irrelevant.

We are also using this opportunity to thank you for the endless patience and support you constantly show for this project. Hopefully, we will be able to come back to you with more details regarding the entire process (and, of course, the finished product) soon!
